scope: Engineering materials, Material Traders, Engineer progression, Remote Workshop, and modern ship-engineering workflow reference knowledge used by the Mongrels Field Manual and Ask the Mongrels.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Engineering materials use a separate inventory: Raw materials run G1-G4; Manufactured and Encoded run G1-G5.
details: Materials use no cargo space or ship mass.
Raw are elemental resources, Manufactured are components/salvage, and Encoded are scan/data resources.
Storage caps per material are G1 300, G2 250, G3 200, G4 150, G5 100; Raw stops at G4.
Normal vehicle destruction does not wipe engineering materials.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use post-18.08 rules: material yields and mission rewards are higher, and blueprint progression is deterministic. At G5 Engineer reputation, G1-G5 take 1/2/3/4/5 rolls.
details: Frontier increased material availability at many G4/G5 sources and increased mission material rewards in August 2024.
Frontier described affected sites rising from roughly 3-6 to roughly 30-100 microresources.
Some mission rewards can reach 24 materials depending on the mission/material limit.
Below G5 Engineer reputation, a blueprint can require more rolls, but the count is no longer random.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use the trader for the correct material family and prefer trading downward. Upgrading or crossing categories is expensive.
details: Raw traders are associated with Refinery/Extraction economies; Manufactured with Extraction/Industrial; Encoded with High Tech/Military.
Traders do not convert Raw into Manufactured or Encoded, or vice versa.
Within one category, trading down one grade gives 3:1; trading up one grade costs 6:1.
Changing material category within the same family adds a 6:1 penalty, and grade/category penalties multiply.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Prioritize strong G4/G5 sources and good mission rewards, then use Material Traders to fill lower grades and awkward gaps.
details: The 2024 rebalance made high-grade locations and mission rewards much more productive than older guides imply.
Avoid cross-trading unless necessary because the penalty is severe.
Check the build/material shopping list first, then target the high-grade branches actually needed.
Keep useful synthesis materials in reserve instead of trading everything to zero.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For G5 Manufactured materials, check High Grade Emissions and mission rewards. Pharmaceutical Isolators are G5 Chemical materials with a higher chance in Outbreak systems.
details: High Grade Emissions are a primary source for several G5 Manufactured materials, and post-18.08 yields are much better than older guides describe.
INARA lists Pharmaceutical Isolators from HGE and mission rewards, with a higher chance in Outbreak states.
Pharmaceutical Isolators are used by G5 Dirty Thrusters engineering.
Use a current component database for the exact state/allegiance association of other HGE materials.

entries.topic: Encoded Sources, Datamined Wake Exceptions & Firmware
entries.ruleOfThumb: Encoded materials come from scans and data points. DWE comes from high-energy wake scans/missions/Encoded Emissions; MEF comes from surface data points and missions.
details: Datamined Wake Exceptions are G5 Encoded Wake Data used in G5 Increased Range FSD engineering.
A Wake Scanner directly collects wake-data materials from high-energy wakes.
Modified Embedded Firmware is G5 Encoded Firmware from surface data points and mission rewards.
Use an Encoded Material Trader to convert surplus encoded data within the family.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Raw materials are elemental resources gathered mainly from planetary surface prospecting and some mining/mission sources. Raw engineering materials stop at G4.
details: Surface deposits, meteorites and crystalline/geological growths are standard Raw-material sources.
Raw materials can also come from asteroid mining and selected mission rewards.
G4 is the highest Raw grade; its per-material storage cap is 150.
Use a Raw Material Trader to trade surplus high-grade elements downward or across raw branches.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Check mission material rewards before farming: post-18.08 payouts are larger, and several useful G5 materials are naturally mission-focused.
details: Frontier increased engineering-material mission rewards, with some payouts reaching up to 24 units.
Biotech Conductors are G5 Manufactured and are listed as mission rewards.
Exquisite Focus Crystals are G5 Manufactured from mission rewards and combat-ship salvage; INARA notes a higher chance in Boom states.
Modified Embedded Firmware is G5 Encoded and can also appear as a mission reward.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Build reputation with each ship Engineer to unlock higher blueprint grades. Remote Workshop modifications do not increase Engineer reputation.
details: Engineer reputation controls access to higher blueprint grades.
Engineering at the Engineer workshop contributes to progression; remote work does not.
Different Engineers specialize in different modules, so unlock planning should follow the modules you actually use.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Pin one blueprint per Engineer for Remote Workshop use. Remote engineering is convenient, but it does not rank up the Engineer.
details: Each Engineer can have one blueprint pinned.
Pinned ship-module blueprints can be used at Remote Workshop services away from the Engineer.
Use pins for frequently repeated blueprints and save Engineer visits for unpinned work and experimentals.

entries.topic: Experimental Effects Require an Engineer Visit
entries.ruleOfThumb: Experimental Effects cannot be applied through Remote Workshop. Apply them at an Engineer workshop that supports the module.
details: A module can carry one Experimental Effect at a time.
Experimentals have a separate one-time material cost.
Remote Workshops cannot apply Experimental Effects.
Changing a module's primary engineering modification can remove the existing experimental, so confirm the final blueprint first.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Plan the build first, generate the material list, fill high-grade bottlenecks, trade for gaps, then visit Engineers for experimentals and unpinned work.
details: Choose the final blueprint and Experimental Effect for each module before spending materials.
Use a build planner/database to identify exact requirements.
Collect high-grade bottlenecks and good mission rewards first, then use Material Traders for lower-grade gaps.
Arrive at the Engineer with both blueprint and separate Experimental Effect materials.
